sources.title: SDLT Manual: rates of tax
sources.verified_claim: SDLT uses marginal rates and depends on chargeable consideration and whether land is residential, non-residential or mixed; candidate liability cannot be calculated without transaction facts.

sources.title: SDLT rates for non-residential and mixed land and property
sources.verified_claim: Non-residential and mixed-property SDLT rates differ from residential rates and apply according to transaction classification and consideration.

sources.title: Higher rates of Stamp Duty Land Tax
sources.verified_claim: Higher residential rates depend on ownership and replacement-main-residence facts; they cannot be assumed from parcel characteristics.

sources.title: Rates of Stamp Duty Land Tax for non-UK residents
sources.verified_claim: A 2 percentage-point surcharge applies to qualifying non-resident residential transactions, subject to detailed residence tests and relief rules.

sources.title: Stamp Duty Land Tax relief for land or property transactions
sources.verified_claim: Multiple statutory reliefs exist and eligibility depends on purchaser, property and transaction facts; no relief is inferred for a candidate.

sources.title: Annual Tax on Enveloped Dwellings
sources.verified_claim: ATED applies to certain high-value UK residential property held by non-natural persons and uses annual charge bands, valuation and relief rules; candidate applicability is unbound.

sources.title: Stamp duty and other tax on property: detailed information
sources.verified_claim: HMRC's current property-tax collection links SDLT, ATED valuation, registration, returns, reliefs and payment guidance; the collection does not establish a candidate tax position.

sources.title: Apply for a refund of Stamp Duty Land Tax
sources.verified_claim: Refund routes exist for specified overpayment, main-home replacement, non-resident surcharge and relief circumstances; refund eligibility requires transaction-specific evidence.
